Also called: posting date, publication date, listing date. Examples: "Job Opening" date posted "2023-10-25", "Apartment for Rent" date posted "2023-10-20", "Public Health Alert" date posted "2023-03-01T09:00:00Z". Distinct from datePublished, which is a more general property for first publication.

candidates.label: category
candidates.comment: A classification relation assigning a category to an item such as an offer, product, service, or announcement. Also called "type", "classification", "genre", "tag". Examples: "Product category 'Electronics'", "Service category 'Home Repair'", "Offer category 'Seasonal Sale'".

candidates.label: releasedEvent
candidates.comment: A released event relation between a creative work and the publication event marking its release. Also called release event, launch event. Examples: "A movie has a released event 'Premiere at Cannes Film Festival'.", "A book has a released event 'Book Launch Party'.", "A video game has a released event 'E3 Announcement'."

candidates.label: releaseDate
candidates.comment: A release date relation between a product and the date it was made available to the public. Also called launch date, availability date, publication date. Examples: "A new smartphone model has a release date of 2024-03-01.", "A software update has a release date of 2023-11-15.", "A new car model has a release date of 2025-01-01.". Distinct from productionDate, which is when the item was manufactured.

candidates.label: availabilityStarts
candidates.comment: A date or time marking the beginning of availability for a product or service in an offer or access specification. Also called: availability start date, offer start, access start time. Examples: "Offer 'New Product' availabilityStarts '2023-11-01'", "ActionAccessSpecification 'Pre-sale' availabilityStarts '2023-10-20T09:00:00'". Distinct from availabilityEnds, which marks the end.

candidates.label: track
candidates.comment: A track relation between a music group or playlist and a music recording, typically a single song. Also called song, musical piece, recording. Examples: "MusicPlaylist track 'Bohemian Rhapsody'", "MusicGroup track 'Stairway to Heaven'", "Album track 'Track 3'". Distinct from tracks, which is a more general property for multiple music recordings.

candidates.label: tracks
candidates.comment: A tracks relation between a music group or playlist and a music recording, typically a single song. Also called song, musical piece, recording. Examples: "MusicPlaylist tracks 'Bohemian Rhapsody'", "MusicGroup tracks 'Stairway to Heaven'", "Album tracks 'Track 3'". Distinct from track, which can also refer to an ItemList of music recordings.

candidates.label: lyrics
candidates.comment: A lyrics relation between a music composition and the creative work containing its words. Also called: song words, text of song, musical text. Examples: "Bohemian Rhapsody lyrics 'Is this the real life? Is this just fantasy?'", "Yesterday lyrics 'Yesterday, all my troubles seemed so far away'", "Hallelujah lyrics 'I've heard there was a secret chord'".

candidates.label: isrcCode
candidates.comment: A music recording identification relation between a music recording and its International Standard Recording Code. Also called ISRC identifier, recording code, music track ID. Examples: A music recording has an isrcCode of 'US-S1Z-99-00001'. A song has an isrcCode of 'GB-LFB-04-00001'. An album track has an isrcCode of 'QZ-F89-12-00001'. Distinct from iswcCode, which is for musical compositions, not recordings.

candidates.label: iswcCode
candidates.comment: A music composition identification relation between a music composition and its International Standard Musical Work Code. Also called ISWC identifier, composition code, musical work ID. Examples: A music composition has an iswcCode of 'T-034.045.001-6'. A song has an iswcCode of 'T-901.234.567-8'. A classical piece has an iswcCode of 'T-123.456.789-0'. Distinct from isrcCode, which is for music recordings, not compositions.

candidates.label: recordingOf
candidates.comment: A recording of relation between a music recording and the music composition it represents. Also called rendition of, version of, based on composition. Examples: "A music recording 'Bohemian Rhapsody' is a recording of 'the Queen composition'.", "A classical track is a recording of 'Beethoven's Symphony No. 9'.", "A cover song is a recording of 'the original composition'.". Distinct from recordedAs, which is the inverse relation.

candidates.label: recordedAs
candidates.comment: A recording relation between a music composition and an audio recording of that work. Also called recorded version, audio rendition. Examples: "A music composition 'Symphony No. 5' is recorded as 'Berlin Philharmonic recording'.", "A song 'Yesterday' is recorded as 'The Beatles' original recording'.", "A classical piece is recorded as 'a live performance album'.". Distinct from recordingOf, which is the inverse relation.

candidates.label: inAlbum
candidates.comment: An album inclusion relation between a music recording and the music album it belongs to. Also called part of album, on album, album track. Examples: "A music recording is in an album titled 'Greatest Hits'.", "The song is in an album.", "This recording belongs to a specific album.". Distinct from inPlaylist, which refers to a music playlist.

candidates.label: inPlaylist
candidates.comment: A playlist inclusion relation between a music recording and the music playlist it belongs to. Also called part of playlist, on playlist, playlist track. Examples: "A music recording is in a playlist titled 'Workout Mix'.", "The song is in a playlist.", "This recording belongs to a specific playlist.". Distinct from inAlbum, which refers to a music album.

candidates.label: hasPart
candidates.comment: A part-whole relation between a creative work and another creative work that is a component of it. Also called includes part, contains component, component of. Examples: "A book has a part that is a chapter.", "A symphony has a part that is a movement.", "A website has a part that is a specific page.". Distinct from includedComposition, which is specific to music compositions.

chosen_property.label: formedIn
chosen_property.definition: To be created or established in a specific year
chosen_property.justification: No existing property fits the meaning of the relation phrase

candidates.label: locationCreated
candidates.comment: A creation location relation between a creative work and the place where it was created. Also called: place of creation, origin location, created in. Examples: "Painting locationCreated Paris", "Novel locationCreated London", "Film locationCreated Hollywood". Distinct from location, which refers to the current or general location of an entity.

candidates.label: foundingLocation
candidates.comment: A founding location relation between an organization and the place where it was established. Also called: place of origin, establishment location, birthplace. Examples: "Microsoft" founding location "Albuquerque, New Mexico", "Apple Inc." founding location "Los Altos, California", "Google" founding location "Menlo Park, California".

candidates.label: foundingDate
candidates.comment: A founding date relation between an organization and the specific date it was established. Also called: establishment date, creation date, inception date. Examples: "Microsoft" founding date "1975-04-04", "Apple Inc." founding date "1976-04-01", "Google" founding date "1998-09-04".

candidates.label: dateCreated
candidates.comment: A temporal origin relation between a creative work or data feed item and the date it was created or added. Also called: creation date, date of origin, initial date. Examples: "Painting" date created "1889-05-01", "Blog Post" date created "2023-03-15T10:00:00Z", "Data Feed Entry" date created "2023-01-01". Distinct from datePublished, which is the date of first public release.

candidates.label: countryOfOrigin
candidates.comment: A provenance relation between a creative work or product and its country of origin. Also called: origin country, produced in, made in. Examples: "French Wine" country of origin "France", "Japanese Anime" country of origin "Japan", "German Car" country of origin "Germany", "Hollywood Movie" country of origin "United States". Distinct from countryOfAssembly, which specifies where the product was put together.

candidates.label: members
candidates.comment: A member relation between an organization or program membership and an organization or person belonging to it. Also called: includes members, comprises, consists of. Examples: "Club Organization members John Doe", "Team ProgramMembership members Jane Smith", "Alliance Organization members Partner Company". Distinct from member, which is a singular form and essentially the same concept.

candidates.label: comprisedOf
candidates.comment: A compositional relation between an anatomical system and the anatomical structures or other systems that physically comprise it. Also called "composed of", "consists of", "includes". Examples: "Circulatory system comprisedOf Heart", "Digestive system comprisedOf Stomach".

candidates.label: founder
candidates.comment: A founder relation between an organization and the person or organization that established it. Also called: established by, created by, initiated by. Examples: "Microsoft" founder "Bill Gates", "Apple Inc." founder "Steve Jobs", "Google" founder "Larry Page". Distinct from founders, which is specifically for multiple people.

candidates.label: hasBioChemEntityPart
candidates.comment: A part-whole relation between a biochemical entity and one of its constituent biochemical entities. Also called composed of, contains, includes part, made of. Examples: "A protein has a BioChemEntity part of an amino acid sequence.", "A cell has BioChemEntity parts like organelles.", "A molecule has BioChemEntity parts of atoms."

candidates.label: founders
candidates.comment: A founders relation between an organization and the people who established it. Also called: co-founders, creators, originators. Examples: "Google" founders "Larry Page, Sergey Brin", "Apple Inc." founders "Steve Jobs, Steve Wozniak, Ronald Wayne", "Microsoft" founders "Bill Gates, Paul Allen". Distinct from founder, which can be a single person or organization.

chosen_property.label: nominatedFor
chosen_property.definition: To be nominated for a specific award
chosen_property.justification: No existing property fits the meaning of the relation phrase

candidates.label: candidate
candidates.comment: A participation relation in a vote action, indicating the person who is being voted for. Also called "voted for", "nominee", "electoral candidate". Examples: "Election vote action candidate Jane Smith", "Award vote action candidate John Doe".

candidates.label: award
candidates.comment: An award won by or for a creative work, organization, person, product, or service. Also called: honor, prize, recognition. Examples: "CreativeWork 'Movie' award 'Oscar'", "Organization 'Company X' award 'Best Employer'", "Person 'Scientist' award 'Nobel Prize'". Distinct from awards, which is the plural form.

candidates.label: awards
candidates.comment: Awards won by or for a creative work, organization, person, or product. Also called: honors, prizes, recognitions. Examples: "CreativeWork 'Movie' awards 'Oscar'", "Organization 'Company X' awards 'Best Employer'", "Person 'Scientist' awards 'Nobel Prize'". Distinct from award, which is the singular form.

candidates.label: reservationFor
candidates.comment: A reservation for relation between a reservation and the specific item or service being booked. Also called booked item, reserved item, subject of reservation. Examples: "A reservation is for 'Flight BA249'.", "A restaurant booking is for 'Dinner at The Fancy Bistro'.", "A hotel reservation is for 'Room 301'."

candidates.label: programMembershipUsed
candidates.comment: A program membership application relation between a reservation and the loyalty program membership used for it. Also called applied membership, loyalty program for, membership applied to. Examples: "A flight reservation used a 'MileagePlus Gold' program membership.", "A hotel reservation used a 'Marriott Bonvoy Platinum' program membership.", "A car rental reservation used an 'Emerald Club' program membership."

candidates.label: recommendationStrength
candidates.comment: A recommendation strength relation between a medical guideline recommendation and its categorized level of evidence or support. Also called strength of evidence, guideline strength. Examples: "A medical guideline recommendation has a recommendation strength 'Class I'.", "A treatment guideline has a recommendation strength 'Strong'.", "A diagnostic recommendation has a recommendation strength 'Grade B'."

candidates.label: eligibleWithSupplier
candidates.comment: An eligible with supplier relation between a financial incentive and the organization that supplies the incentivized item or service. Also called "supplier partner", "incentive provider", "valid with retailer". Examples: "Rebate eligibleWithSupplier 'Utility Company X'", "Discount eligibleWithSupplier 'Electronics Store Y'", "Grant eligibleWithSupplier 'Solar Panel Installer Z'".

candidates.label: winner
candidates.comment: A winner relation between a losing action and the person who won it. Also called victor, triumphant participant, successful party. Examples: ChessMatchLoseAction winner Alice, RaceLoseAction winner Bob, CompetitionLoseAction winner Charlie.

candidates.label: hasCredential
candidates.comment: A credential relation between an organization or person and an awarded credential. Also called holds credential, awarded credential, possesses credential. Examples: "A person has a credential as a licensed engineer.", "An organization has a credential for business excellence.", "The professional has a credential in data science."

candidates.label: eligibleDuration
candidates.comment: An eligible duration relation between a demand or offer and the quantitative value representing the period for which it is valid. Also called "validity period", "offer duration", "term length". Examples: "Offer 'Limited Time Sale' eligibleDuration 'P7D'", "Subscription offer eligibleDuration 'P1Y'", "Demand 'Project Bid' eligibleDuration 'P30D'".
